walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Discarded computers, phones and other electronic devices are known as:
options: Freeware
E-waste
Open data
Greyware
How organisations collect, store and use personal data
The speed of broadband connections
Who may buy a computer
The price of software licences

mcqs.q: Which of these is an ENVIRONMENTAL impact of computing?
options: Cyberbullying on social media
Software piracy
The energy consumed by large data centres
Phishing emails

mcqs.q: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 makes it illegal to:
options: Access computer material without authorisation
Sell second-hand computers
Store any personal data
Use open-source software

mcqs.q: Is an issue automatically ethical rather than legal just because it involves computers?
options: Yes - e-waste is harmless because devices are switched off.
Yes - laws cannot apply to anything done online.
No - hacking and data misuse are LEGAL issues covered by specific laws, while questions the law does not settle, like algorithmic bias, are ethical issues.
Yes - all computing issues are ethical because technology is new.
Yes - e-waste is harmless because devices are switched off.
No - much e-waste ends up in landfill or is exported, where toxic materials like lead and mercury can harm people and the environment.
Yes - laws cannot apply to anything done online.
Yes - every old device handed in is fully and safely recycled.

mcqs.q: Does data protection law mean companies can never share your data?
options: Yes - any sharing of personal data is automatically illegal.
Yes - companies may only share data with the government.
Yes - e-waste is harmless because devices are switched off.
No - data can be shared when there is a lawful basis, such as your consent or a contract; the law regulates sharing rather than banning it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “E-waste”?
options: A question about whether a use of technology is morally right, such as monitoring employees or using algorithms to make decisions about people.
A matter governed by law, such as data protection, computer misuse and copyright, where breaking the rules can lead to prosecution.
Discarded electronic devices, which contain toxic substances and valuable materials, creating pollution when dumped rather than properly recycled.
The inequality between people who have good access to digital technology and skills and those who do not.

options: The inequality between people who have good access to digital technology and skills and those who do not.
Discarded electronic devices, which contain toxic substances and valuable materials, creating pollution when dumped rather than properly recycled.
A person's ability to control who collects, sees and uses information about them, challenged by tracking, cameras and data-hungry apps.
A question about whether a use of technology is morally right, such as monitoring employees or using algorithms to make decisions about people.
